scope: Bind a generated CAMERA's nonzero code-340 view reference to the exact emitted VIEW table row, with fail-closed behavior for missing and wrong-kind targets.

references.title: Autodesk DXF Group Codes in Numerical Order Reference
references.use: Defines group codes 340-349 as hard-pointer handles. The exact CAMERA-to-VIEW relation is bounded here by the current libdxfrw model/parser mapping and generated output/readback; this generic table alone does not qualify native CAMERA semantics.

behavior: DXF VIEW serialization binds a non-null source table handle to its emitted handle and records the exact VIEW-row role within the record transaction; rollback removes both bindings.

CAMERA serialization requires the exact DRW_Camera runtime class and DRW::CAMERA public tag, then emits group 340 only when the source handle was completed by the VIEW writer in the current output attempt; it writes the emitted handle rather than the source handle.

Missing targets, references to non-VIEW table rows, a late missing target after another VIEW row has been serialized, derived runtime classes, and mismatched public tags are refused before publication.

validationProfile.source: Locally constructed DRW_View and DRW_Camera models; output files are temporary and no drawing fixture is committed.
assertions: A missing VIEW target is refused and an existing destination remains byte-identical.
A LAYER row with the same source handle does not satisfy the CAMERA VIEW reference.
An unrelated VIEW is serialized before the missing-reference refusal; the destination remains unchanged and the same adapter retries successfully after adding the correct target.
A derived DRW_Camera and a base CAMERA tagged as another entity type are each refused atomically; restoring the exact class/tag permits corrected same-adapter retry.
Fresh typed import verifies that CAMERA.m_viewHandle equals the emitted handle of CAMERA_TARGET_VIEW.

validation.focusedTestResult: PASS: 1/1 in ASCII and Binary DXF.

limitations: Generated transport evidence only; no independent physical CAMERA producer or native application behavior is qualified.
The route does not qualify camera projection, rendering, or broader 3D geometry semantics.
No support claim is promoted; P8 remains open.
